findings.text: test_members_query_compares_every_invariant_segment asserts set(_compared_columns(_PATTERN_FAMILY_MEMBERS_QUERY)) == set(PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS), but _PATTERN_FAMILY_MEMBERS_QUERY is generated from that same constant through _invariant_equality (families.py:457), so the assertion's two sides move together: dropping a segment from PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS drops it from the query too and this test stays green. It guards only an independent edit to the query generator, not the constant it names; the behavioural guard for the entity column is the entity-owner control.

the fetch_sibling_family docstring still states the invariant segments are physical_base, geometric_base, transformation and process and lists the variation axes without geometry, contradicting the code beneath it, which now holds object invariant and geometry varying; a reader of the changed function is told the old rule.

the census prose says 'The locus rule is read from the ISN registry (load_locus_registry())', but production pattern_signature and PATTERN_INVARIANT_SEGMENTS (families.py:417,524) hard-code the segment set; only the test at tests/standard_names/test_pattern_families.py:221 reads the registry, so the record misstates the landed mechanism.

the after_suite entry claims 87 passed over six files while its cited log logs/after_suite.log records 83 passed over five (tests/graph/test_cypher_property_check.py ran separately, logs/cypher_property_check.log, 4 passed); the JSON also uses non-canonical keys (files/passed/failed/exit/rev/log) with no command or failure_ids, so a schema reader sees an unreadable suite arm even though zero added failures is the true reading.

build_worklist re-implements the invariant projection string inline (coalesce(c.{seg}, '') AS {seg}) instead of reusing families.py:449 _invariant_projection, so the projection expression — though not the segment list — is still stated in two places and can drift.

the docs prompt renders item.sibling_family.parent.name unguarded (also refine_docs_user.md:64 and review_docs_user.md:80); the landed change makes parent None when the base token names no node (context.py:859), so such a render now yields an empty parent anchor.
